# Seal Claude Local Guide

## Mission

Seal is a Vortex company repo. Ship the active limiter, delete stale process, and keep project truth in this repo so local and cloud agents start from the same facts.

## First Actions

- Run `bun run repo:status` from the repo root.
- Read AGENTS.md and any subdirectory AGENTS.md before touching code.
- Read .test-env before live proof or dev-server work.
- Attack the single active limiter; do not broaden payments, auth, or docs scope without evidence.

## Algorithm

1. Question every requirement. Name the person or repo fact behind it.
2. Delete. Remove stale instructions, duplicate config, dead code, and hand-maintained process.
3. Simplify. Only simplify what survived deletion.
4. Accelerate. Shorten the loop after the work is real.
5. Automate last. Do not automate a broken process.

## Hard Rules

- Use bun only. Do not use npm, yarn, pnpm, or npx.
- Never use the `any` type. Use `unknown` and narrow it.
- Never add `eslint-disable`, `biome-ignore`, Ultracite, or other stale local lint bypasses.
- Use Core-owned tooling through repo scripts: `bun run lint`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run check:preferred-stack`, and `bun run repo:check` when available.
- No AI attribution in commits, PRs, generated files, or release notes.
- No worktrees. Branch from `staging` and PR back to `staging`.
- Do not release or version-bump for refactors. Release only for a closed gate or named consumer need.
- Browser E2E is release-only. Do not run Playwright, `test:e2e`, `agent-browser`, or `vb` from routine PR/push CI.

## Vortex Auth

- Auth package: `@vortexnyc/auth`
- Convex dir: `apps/backend/convex`
- Run `bun run auth:check` before changing auth-owned org/member/role/invitation data.
- Run `bun run auth:preflight` after install/env/runtime changes and before auth UI or rollout work.
- Do not build an app-local auth engine. The consumer owns adapter glue; Core owns auth semantics.

## Cloud Sessions

Cloud agents clone only this repo. Assume there is no sibling checkout, no global Codex or Claude config, no local secrets file, no 1Password, no Touch ID, and no interactive browser login unless the environment explicitly provides it.

- Preserve root AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md because they contain Seal-specific navigation and design context.
- Use staging for Vortex payments, subscriptions, webhooks, billing, and payment verification.
- Do not target the retired self-hosted Convex URLs.

## Local Sessions

Local agents may inspect sibling Vortex repos for existing patterns, but only when the checkout exists locally and the work does not cross a forbidden touch zone.

- Read .test-env before live proof; it is the local source of truth for dev URLs and deployments.
- Use vb or vb --fresh against TEST_WEB_URL for browser proof.
- Do not reopen payments migration scope unless the active task explicitly requires it.

Reference repos:

- vortex-core for shared auth/tooling contracts
- crm for the current clean Vortex Core consumer proof

## Design Context

- Seal is a workflow-focused document signing and collaboration app for B2B teams.
- Prioritize reliability, speed, clear task completion, and high trust over decorative UI.
- Use packages/tokens for brand colors, typography, status colors, signer slots, motion, and form affordances.
- Support light and dark themes with practical, restrained motion.
